items.text: Isaiah’s prophecies were meant to comfort the Jewish people, but they reach even further into the future, speaking to us who also sometimes feel defeated, disheartened, and even lost. The Lord’s message is simple: 'Fear not.' All is not lost; He has power over situations that seem out of your control.

The Lord, who created the heavens, is more powerful than Babylon, than sin, than whatever is holding you captive. He pleads, 'Return unto me, for I have redeemed thee.' He can heal, restore, strengthen, forgive, and comfort—whatever is needed for you to be redeemed.

When the Israelites were captives in Babylon, many wondered if they had lost their place as God’s chosen people. As you read Isaiah 40–49, look for passages that provided comfort and hope, and ponder what the Lord might be saying to you personally in these verses.

The Lord declared, 'I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee.' He is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not faint, nor be weary, and His understanding is unsearchable. Trust in His power and everlasting love for you.

The Lord is the Creator of the heavens and the earth. He has declared that He has redeemed and called us by name. We are His. He promises to be with us in our troubles, to deliver us, and to give us honor and glory.

The Lord proclaims, 'I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sins.' He invites us to return unto Him, for He has redeemed us. He will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert.

The Lord reminds us, 'Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord.' We are called to share the good tidings of the gospel. Imagine testifying in a trial that Jesus Christ is the Savior and the Redeemer, presenting evidence from your life to support His claims.

The Lord has called us to serve Him and has 'formed' and prepared us for this purpose. He supports us as we serve, even when our efforts seem 'for nought, and in vain.' He has chosen us and will not cast us off.

The Lord’s promises can bring peace. By obeying Him, we can have 'peace … as a river.' This peace flows from His power and His commitment to us, His covenant people, even through trials and tribulations.

The Lord promises to be our everlasting strength and our guide. He will not leave us nor forsake us. Even when we feel weak or lost, His power is infinite, and His love is unending. We can rely on Him to help us through every challenge.
